newsitem.title: UK: Wessex on course for targets to cut leaks.
newsitem.headline: Wessex on course for targets to cut leaks.

text.p: Britain's Wessex Water Plc said on Wednesday it was on course to meet a target of cutting leaks to 15 percent of supplies which should allow it to meet "any sensible mandatory targets."
The water utility turned in year pretax profits of 145 million pounds ($241.9 million), up eight percent, and paid out a total dividend of 18 pence per share, compared with 15.2 pence.

The new Labour government has said it will introduce mandatory targets for cutting leakage as part of a 10-point plan to cope with the country's current drought, the worst in 200 years, as well as a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities.
Wessex said a combination of cuts in leakage and water conservation should enable it to hold overall consumption "at, or near, current levels."
The company said its diversified businesses were doing well with its UK Waste waste management company "positioned for further profit growth."
It said it was in "an excellent position to continue delivering growing shareholder value."
